questions.question: Nathu La Pass connects India with which of its neighbouring countries?
questions.questionHtml: Nathu La Pass connects India with which of its neighbouring countries?
questions.solution: The Nathu La Pass, located at 14,450 feet in the East Sikkim district, is a significant Himalayan pass connecting India with China's Tibet Autonomous Region. It is one of the highest motorable roads globally and part of the Old Silk Route. Nathu La, meaning 'listening ears' (Nathu) and 'pass' (La), was closed for nearly 40 years following a Tibetan uprising in 1959 and reopened in 2006. It serves as a vital trading border post and an official Border Personnel Meeting (BPM) Point, known for its scenic beauty. Other notable Himalayan passes include Zoji La, Banihal Pass, Shipki La, Bara-Lacha La, Mana Pass, and Niti Pass.

questions.solution: The Grand Trunk Road, one of South Asia's oldest and longest major roads, extends from Amritsar to Kolkata in India. Built by Sher Shah Suri in the 16<sup>th</sup> century, it starts in Kabul and continues through Pakistan's Khyber Pass. The road was built to connect the east and west regions of the Indian subcontinent during British colonial rule.

questions.question: Which National Waterway is associated with the Brahmaputra River?
questions.questionHtml: Which National Waterway is associated with the Brahmaputra River?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is National Waterway 2.

Key Points

  • National Waterway 2 (NW-2) is a 891 km long stretch on the Brahmaputra River in Assam.
  • This waterway extends from Dhubri to Sadiya in the state of Assam.
  • It was declared as National Waterway 2 in 1988 under the National Waterways Act.
  • NW-2 is significant for the transportation of cargo and passengers, contributing to the economic development of the region.

Additional Information

  • National Waterways in India:
    • India has a total of 111 National Waterways declared under the National Waterways Act, 2016.
    • These waterways are intended to promote and develop inland water transport.
  • Inland Water Transport:
    • It is a mode of transport where goods and passengers are transported via navigable rivers, canals, and backwaters.
    • This mode of transportation is cost-effective and environmentally friendly.
  • Significance of NW-2:
    • NW-2 serves as a major waterway for trade and commerce in the Northeast region of India.
    • It plays a crucial role in the transportation of tea, coal, petroleum products, and other goods.
  • Challenges:
    • Challenges such as seasonal variations in water levels and the need for regular dredging impact the effectiveness of inland water transport.
    • Infrastructure development and maintenance are critical for the efficient operation of these waterways.

questions.questionHtml: The ______ in China is the world’s longest man-made waterway.
questions.solution:
• The Grand Canal in China is the world’s longest man-made waterway.
  • The Grand Canal starts in Beijing and ends at the city of Hangzhou in Zhejiang province. It connects the Yellow River with the Yangtze River.
  • It is one of the world’s largest and most comprehensive civil engineering projects prior to the Industrial Revolution.
  • The length of the Grand Canal is around 1800 km which makes it the world's longest manmade waterway.
  • It is declared as World Heritage Site by UNESCO.

questions.question: According to their capacity, roads are classified into how many classes in India?
questions.questionHtml: According to their capacity, roads are classified into how many classes in India?
questions.solution: India has six types of roads - National Highways, State Highways, District roads, Rural roads, Border Roads, and Expressways. They connect different areas and are built and maintained by different authorities. National Highways and State Highways are the most important ones.

questions.question: In how many classes are roads classified in India?
questions.questionHtml: In how many classes are roads classified in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Six'

Key Points

  • The roads are classified into six types: National Highways, State Highways, District roads, Rural roads, Border Roads, and Expressways.
  • National Highways are the roads that connect one state with another and also connect important ports. These roads are constructed and laid by the Central Public Works Department(CPWD). They are designated with NH.
  • State Highways are highways connecting major cities all over the state, it also connects other state highways of neighbouring states. It is designated by SH. State governments have the authority to build and maintain highways. Constructed and maintained by Public Work Departments of state.
  • District roads are the roads where the districts are connected to each other. Other than a district, Zila Parishads also have the authority and responsibility to build roads.
  • Rural roads are single-lane roads used to connect India's rural and remote areas. The roads are constructed and laid by Panchayats or by the project of Pradhan Mantri Gramin Sadak Yojna(PMGSY)
  • Border roads are the roads constructed on the North and North Eastern borders of the country, constructed and maintained by the Border Roads Organization (BRO).
  • Expressways are high-speed roads that are four or more lanes that have been designed for high-speed vehicular traffic, with all traffic flow regulated with toll roads. National Expressways Authority of India operates under the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.

Additional Information

  • The minister for the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways is Nitin Gadkari.
  • Pradhan Mantri Gramin Sadak Yojna(PMGSY) was launched in December 2000, by the Indian Government to provide connectivity to isolated rural habitations.
  • Border Road Organisation was set up in 1960 by the Government of India, it is regarded as the symbol of nation building, national integration and maintaining the security of the country.

questions.question: In which year was the Konkan Railway constructed?
questions.questionHtml: In which year was the Konkan Railway constructed?
questions.solution: The Konkan Railway was constructed in 1998 and is a major railway project in India, connecting the western coast with the rest of the country. It spans the regions of Maharashtra, Goa, and Karnataka, playing a crucial role in transportation and trade.

questions.question: National Waterways 10 (NW-10) is located in which state?
questions.questionHtml: National Waterways 10 (NW-10) is located in which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

Key Points

  • India has a vast network of inland waterways that include river bodies, canals, backwaters and creeks.
  • According to the National Waterways Act, 2016, 111 inland waterways (including five national waterways in India declared earlier) have been declared as ‘national waterways’.
  • Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI), a statutory authority in charge of the waterways in India, is responsible for the timely execution of national waterways projects and to ensure improved water transportation in India.
  • Out of the 111 National Waterways (NWs) declared under the National Waterways Act, of 2016, 13 NWs are operational for shipping and navigation and cargo/passenger vessels are moving on them.

questions.question: In India, roads are classified in the _____ classes according to their capacity.
questions.questionHtml: In India, roads are classified in the _____ classes according to their capacity.
questions.solution: Road classification in India is based on capacity, considering lanes, width, and design. There are six classes, ranging from expressways (Class 1) to rural roads (Class 6). This classification aids infrastructure planning. Recommendations by the Indian Roads Congress guide road development, ensuring connectivity from major cities to villages and individual homes.

questions.question: Which among the following is India's first corporatized port?
questions.questionHtml: Which among the following is India's first corporatized port?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Ennore.

Key Points According to the Ministry of Ports, Shipping, and Waterways, around 95 percent of India's trading by volume and 70 percent by value is done through maritime transport. It is serviced by 13 major ports (12 Government-owned and one private) and 187 notified minor and intermediate ports.

First corporatized port of India:

  • Kamarajar port located at Ennore in Tamil Nadu is the only corporate port owned by the Indian government.
  • Kamarajar Port Ltd was formed as a company under the Companies Act when it was opened in 2001.
  • Ennore Port is located on the Coromandel Coast about 18 km north of Chennai Port, Chennai, it is the 12th major port of India.
  • It is the first port in India which is a public company.
  • The Kamarajar Port Limited is the only corporatized major port and is registered as a company.

Additional Information

Corporatized port of India:

  • The process of corporatization means that there is a change in legal structure.
  • It should not be confused with privatization or disinvestment.
  • Thus, no major impact can be expected by a mere change in the legal structure.
  • Under the Major Port Trusts Act of 1963, the ports trusts are managed by the Boards of Trustees.
  • Major Port Authorities Bill 2020 was recently introduced in the Lok Sabha by the Ministry of Shipping.
  • The Bill aims to replace the Major Port Trusts Act, 1963.
  • It seeks to provide for the regulation, operation, and planning of Major Ports in India and to vest the administration, control, and management of such ports upon the Boards of Major Port Authorities.
  • This will empower the Major Ports to perform with greater efficiency on account of full autonomy in decision making and by modernizing the institutional framework of Major Ports.

questions.question: Through which of the following states does the National Waterway-96 pass?
questions.questionHtml: Through which of the following states does the National Waterway-96 pass?
questions.solution: National Waterway-96 passes through Odisha. It is located on the Subaranekha river and its length is 314 km. questions.question: When was ‘Vayudoot’ airline setup in India?
questions.questionHtml: When was ‘Vayudoot’ airline setup in India?
questions.solution: Vayudoot was established in India in 1981 as a joint venture between Indian Airlines and Air India. It was headquartered at New Delhi's Safdarjung Airport and primarily served the Northeastern part of India. The airline was set up to operate as a regional airline to improve air connectivity in the region. Therefore, the correct answer is 1981.

questions.question: Under the National Waterways Act, 2016, how many inland waterways have been declared as 'national waterways'?
questions.questionHtml: Under the National Waterways Act, 2016, how many inland waterways have been declared as 'national waterways'?
questions.solution: 111 inland waterways have been declared as 'national waterways' under the National Waterways Act, 2016. The National Waterways Act, 2016 was enacted to provide for the development, maintenance, and regulation of inland waterways for navigation and shipping.
